- User-approved merge to protected `main` triggers the single verify → immutable build → private deploy → exact-revision smoke DAG.
- Prove the deployed version/health corresponds to the merge commit or artifact digest.
- Do not expose the origin publicly in Core.
- Cloudflare, domain selection, private Git configuration, and public hosted access remain Extended work.

### Submission package

- Comprehensive README: setup, use-case rationale, workflow, demo, API usage, testing, design decisions, security boundaries, trade-offs, limitations, and troubleshooting.
- Architecture overview finalized from PR #7.
- “What next” writeup maps MVP Extended/Future work and production hardening.
- Assessment matrix in PRD/release issue links exact evidence.
- Meaningful Git history review.
- Exact command, CI run URL, deployment SHA/digest, read-only RBAC, and demo evidence.
- Complete AI interaction inventory and full secret-reviewed exports for every user-facing session and delegated-agent prompt, relevant interaction, result, owner review, correction, and final outcome. Summaries do not replace full available transcripts. Use an explicit redaction manifest when needed, and carry forward any evidence blocker found by the #8 preflight.
- Useful screenshots or short recording for UI stages/outcomes if time remains.
- Final known-risk and failed-gate record.

## Non-goals

- Cloudflare or public-domain exposure.
- Private repository configuration or CRUD.
- CPU/memory resource drift.
- Cancellation, retry, timeout status, discovery, in-cluster DriftLens, or Extended scope.
- Production HA, backups, audit retention, or multi-user authentication.

## Acceptance criteria

- A clean clone completes the documented local setup.
- DriftLens UI and API execute a real read-only GitHub-to-kind scan.
- All four comparison/demo scenarios and actionable failure/recovery are retained in history.
- Replica and image differences are exact; extra live sidecars remain ignored if demonstrated/tested.
- Manual AI explanation works for a completed outcome; deterministic truth remains unchanged.
- Dedicated kubeconfig fails attempted Deployment mutation while required read succeeds.
- Full local quality pyramid passes on the final exact head.
- Protected-main merge automatically deploys and smoke-verifies the exact revision privately.
- README, architecture, trade-offs, next-work, API, demo, and security documentation are complete.
- Every assessment requirement in #3 links retained evidence.
- Complete secret-safe user-facing and delegated-agent interaction exports are present, including prompts, available interaction/tool records, results, owner reviews, corrections, and final outcomes; summaries are not substituted for required full logs.
- The session inventory reconciles every delegation to an export location or an explicitly recorded submission blocker.
- Final repository secret scan and dependency audit pass.

## Test and evidence requirements

- Unit: happy, edge, and failure coverage for every changed module.
- Integration: SQLite/API contracts plus the one authorized real kind proof.
- End-to-end: one-worker, zero-retry Chromium critical operator flow.
- Security: read-only RBAC denial proof, workflow trust audit, credential/log/export scan.
- Delivery: GitHub Actions URLs, exact source SHA, artifact identity, deployment health/version, and rollback note.
- Documentation: commands executed from a clean clone or equivalent isolated checkout.

## Documentation

This issue owns the final README, demo guide, next-work writeup, assessment evidence index, AI-export inventory, and known-limitations/risk record.

## Rollback and teardown

Redeploy the last known-good immutable artifact if smoke fails. Preserve the SQLite evidence file unless corruption requires user-directed recovery. Demo-cluster teardown is explicit and targets only the named disposable cluster. Runner, environment, DNS, credential, or other control-plane deletion requires explicit user approval.

{"body":"## Goal

Create the smallest runnable DriftLens foundation and prove that only trusted canonical-repository pushes can use the self-hosted CI/deployment path.

Parent: #3
Architecture: #4 and PR #7
Target budget: 18 active minutes, recalculated before implementation.

## Operator value

A clean clone runs a recognizable DriftLens shell with health, readiness, and version evidence. Every later issue inherits a working test/build/container/deployment path rather than deferring integration risk.

## Scope

### Application scaffold

- Next.js App Router with TypeScript strict mode and npm lockfile.
- Node 24 pinned consistently for local, CI, and deployment.
- Minimal focused-console shell; no product workflow UI yet.
- Health, readiness, and immutable build-version API responses.
- Environment validation with safe actionable errors.
- ESLint, strict type check, Vitest, coverage command, production build, and dependency audit scripts.
- Multi-stage Docker image and minimal configuration for the reused Proxmox/Cloudflare-protected runtime.
- Baseline README instructions for install, checks, build, and local start.

### Trusted GitHub Actions path

- One workflow family triggered only by `push` in `RGCsAGupta/driftlens`.
- Trusted issue branches run verify: install, lint, type, unit, build, audit, and secret scan.
- `main` continues in the same run to immutable image/build, deployment through the existing Proxmox/Cloudflare-protected path, and exact-version health smoke.
- Deployment uses one non-cancelling concurrency group.
- Workflow token permissions are read-only by default.
- Every third-party Action is pinned to a full commit SHA.
- No `pull_request`, `pull_request_target`, issue-comment, fork, external-contributor, or automatic dependency-bot execution on self-hosted runners.

### Existing environment audit and reuse

Begin with a read-only inventory of the existing [REDACTED: PRIVATE TOPOLOGY] self-hosted execution environment, isolated CI/deployment identities, deployment permissions, and Cloudflare-protected route. Reuse working configuration; do not recreate or replace it.

The live DriftLens repository currently has no registered repository runner and no private demo deployment environment, so verify whether only repository binding is missing. If reuse requires a new runner host, execution identity, credential, permission expansion, or replacement of working configuration, stop and request a separate user decision.

### Repository controls

Approval of this specification authorizes only verified missing DriftLens repository bindings and controls:

- bind the existing isolated [REDACTED: PRIVATE TOPOLOGY] CI and deployment execution environments to DriftLens as required;
- verify CI cannot access deployment kubeconfig, Cloudflare credentials, or broad home-lab resources;
- verify and reuse the existing Cloudflare route and access policy without creating or expanding either;
- bind existing deployment permissions through a DriftLens environment restricted to `main`, without creating broader authority;
- protect `main` against direct push, force-push, and deletion;
- require pull requests and the verified branch check before merge; and
- retain the user as the only write principal unless the user explicitly adds a collaborator.

Registration tokens and credentials must never enter logs, prompts, issues, PRs, commits, or AI exports.

### AI interaction evidence preflight

Before delegating implementation, verify that the export process preserves each delegated-agent prompt, relevant interaction, result, owner review, correction, and final outcome. Start the session inventory and secret-review procedure. If the platform export omits delegated interactions and no complete separate export is available, do not delegate implementation and record the evidence blocker.

## Non-goals

- Scan workflow, GitHub manifest loading, Kubernetes access, SQLite history, or OpenAI.
- New public DNS, a new or expanded Cloudflare route/access policy, or a new Proxmox environment.
- Kubernetes deployment of DriftLens.
- Product UI beyond a recognizable shell.
- External-contributor CI.

## Acceptance criteria

- Clean clone succeeds with documented Node 24 and npm commands.
- Local UI, health, readiness, and build-version endpoints run.
- Lint, type, unit, coverage, production build, dependency audit, and secret scan pass.
- Docker image builds and reports the injected exact commit SHA.
- DriftLens is bound to the verified existing isolated self-hosted execution environments without recreating working host-side configuration.
- A canonical issue-branch push runs verify without deployment access.
- Fork/PR/comment triggers cannot schedule a self-hosted job by workflow inspection and repository settings.
- `main` protection blocks direct pushes and requires the verified check.
- A user-approved merge push runs verify, build, deployment through the reused protected path, and exact-revision smoke without a second approval.
- The protected endpoint reports the exact merged revision, and direct origin bypass is unavailable.
- No secret or sensitive home-lab value appears in retained evidence.
- AI export preflight proves delegated interactions can be completely captured and secret-reviewed before any implementation delegation.

## Test evidence

- Happy: local and container health/version checks pass.
- Edge: missing non-secret required configuration produces a safe readiness failure.
- Failure: a deliberately failing unit check blocks build/deploy in a controlled test or workflow-level fixture; do not merge broken code.
- Security: workflow-event audit proves no externally triggerable self-hosted event and deployment credentials are unavailable to verify jobs.

## Documentation

Update README foundation setup, required non-secret variables, check commands, the reused protected deployment path, and its limitations. Record exact runner labels only if they reveal no sensitive infrastructure detail.

## Dependencies

- User-approved architecture issue #4.
- PR #7 merged before this implementation PR is ready.
- [REDACTED: PRIVATE TOPOLOGY] access and existing host-side and Cloudflare-protected deployment prerequisites.

## Rollback

Redeploy the last known-good immutable artifact. Revert repository setting changes only with explicit user approval. Remove a runner registration only after confirming no active job and preserving evidence.

{"body":"## Goal

Deliver the first complete product workflow: start one real read-only scan from configured GitHub desired state to a live Kubernetes Deployment, persist progress/history, and retrieve exact deterministic results through the API.

Parent: #3
Architecture: #4 and PR #7
Depends on: #8
Target budget: 52 active minutes, recalculated before implementation.

## Operator value

A platform engineer can determine through independently accessible APIs whether the configured Deployment is in sync, drifted in replicas/images, or missing, while retaining actionable state and failures.

## Scope

### Server configuration

- One configured public GitHub `owner/repository` and safe relative YAML manifest path.
- One server-configured kubeconfig path and optional explicit context.
- Configuration is validated at startup and exposed only as non-secret source metadata.
- API accepts a branch or commit SHA per scan and records the resolved immutable SHA.

### API capabilities

- Start a scan and return `202` with scan identity and queued status.
- Retrieve one scan with status, stage transitions, target, resolved SHA, outcome, differences, and safe error.
- List bounded newest-first history with a default limit and enforced maximum.
- Return a structured conflict while another scan is active.
- Return non-secret configured source metadata needed by the UI.

Exact paths and Zod schemas are defined in the implementation and documented in the PR/README.

### Workflow

Persist and expose:

1. queued;
2. loading desired manifest;
3. reading live Deployment;
4. comparing supported fields;
5. saving result; and
6. completed or failed.

Use self-hosted Next.js `after()` for the in-process task. A simple in-memory coordinator admits at most one active scan in the current process and returns conflict for a second request. There is no automatic retry, cancellation, overall workflow timeout, concurrent-scan support, advanced locking, or restart resumability. Every external transport call has a bounded timeout.

### Desired state

- Resolve branch/SHA through GitHub REST.
- Fetch exactly one file at the resolved SHA.
- Plain YAML, one document, one `apps/v1` Deployment.
- Require explicit name and namespace.
- Reject unsafe path, wrong kind/version, multiple documents, or malformed manifest.

### Live state and comparison

- Read exactly the matching namespaced Deployment with `@kubernetes/client-node`.
- Use read-only Kubernetes access; perform no list/watch/write operation.
- Compare `spec.replicas`, defaulting omitted desired replicas to `1`.
- Match desired regular containers by name and compare exact image strings.
- Desired container missing live reports drift.
- Extra live-only containers are ignored.
- Init/ephemeral containers and unrelated/runtime-owned fields are ignored.
- Produce only `IN_SYNC`, `DRIFTED`, or `MISSING_LIVE` as comparison outcomes.
- Git, manifest, authorization, availability, timeout, and internal failures produce typed execution errors, never drift.

### Persistence

Use Node 24 `node:sqlite` with one idempotent schema-version-1 `PRAGMA user_version` bootstrap, one connection, a scan record, and append-only stage records. All dynamic values use prepared, parameterized statements; only fixed schema bootstrap statements may execute as static SQL.

Persist only PRD-approved projections, differences, timestamps, resolved SHA, outcome, and safe errors. Never persist complete manifests, kubeconfig, credentials, or unrelated fields.

A bootstrap or initial scan write failure releases the in-memory coordinator, returns a safe synchronous service error, and creates no scan. After the queued scan is persisted, terminal failure persistence is best effort: if SQLite itself cannot write the terminal record, readiness, correlated structured logs, and the API expose a safe storage failure without claiming that failed history was durably recorded. Core does not resume the stale workflow automatically.

The coordinator exists only in the current process. Restart clears that marker; any prior `QUEUED` or `RUNNING` record remains unchanged as evidence. Core does not resume, complete, delete, or otherwise recover it, and the new process may start a new scan.

## Non-goals

- Operator workflow UI beyond API inspection.
- AI explanation.
- CPU or memory quantities.
- Configuration CRUD or private Git.
- Detailed event log, cancellation, retry, timeout status, or restart recovery.
- Discovery, scheduling, remediation, or additional Kubernetes resources.
- Live kind proof; the release issue supplies the single bounded live demo.

## Acceptance criteria

- Starting a valid scan returns immediately and stage/status polling observes persisted progress.
- Branch input resolves and stores its immutable commit SHA.
- `IN_SYNC` is exact for matching replicas and every desired container image.
- Replica drift, image drift, and missing desired containers produce field-level differences.
- Extra live-only containers do not produce drift.
- Kubernetes 404 becomes `MISSING_LIVE` and a completed scan.
- Invalid manifest, unsupported resource, Git failure, Kubernetes denial/unavailability, and transport timeout are actionable persisted execution failures when storage remains available.
- Bootstrap/initial-scan storage failure returns synchronously without a scan; later storage failure is exposed safely without a false durable-history claim.
- History survives application restart and returns bounded newest-first results.
- A concurrent start attempt returns conflict without creating a second active workflow.
- After restart, the new in-memory coordinator admits a new scan and leaves any stale prior record unchanged.
- API responses and logs contain no credentials or complete manifests.

## Test evidence

- Unit happy: replicas/images in sync.
- Unit edges: omitted replicas, name-based reordered containers, extra live sidecar ignored, missing desired container, multiple differences.
- Unit failures: malformed/multi-document/wrong-resource manifest and safe error mapping.
- Workflow happy: fake GitHub/Kubernetes adapters drive every stage to persisted completion.
- Workflow failures: each adapter/stage failure persists the correct terminal error; no automatic retry calls occur.
- Persistence: version-1 bootstrap idempotency, prepared-statement binding, injection-safe dynamic values, ordered stages, restart history, and bounded query.
- Storage failures: bootstrap/initial-scan failure creates no scan; later write failure proves best-effort terminal handling plus safe readiness, log, and API evidence.
- Restart coordinator: a new process can start a scan while the stale prior record remains neither resumed, completed, deleted, nor modified.
- API: validation, `202`, polling detail, history, not-found, and active conflict.
- Security: fake Kubernetes client asserts read-only Deployment operation and sanitized persistence/logging.

## Documentation

Document non-secret configuration, API capability examples, comparison semantics, error taxonomy, persistence boundary, and Core limitations.

## Rollback

Revert the application commit and redeploy the last known-good artifact. Database bootstrap must be backward-safe for this issue; if a schema rollback is unsafe, preserve the file and document recovery rather than deleting history.

{"body":"## Goal

Allow the operator to manually request and persist a short structured explanation for every completed comparison outcome without letting AI determine or alter drift.

Parent: #3
Architecture: #4 and PR #7
Depends on: #8, #9, and #10
Target budget: 14 active minutes, recalculated before implementation.

## Operator value

An operator receives concise analysis of deterministic differences, implications, investigation checks, and uncertainty while retaining the exact field-level result as source of truth.

## Scope

### Explanation API and state

- Add a manual explanation request capability for completed `IN_SYNC`, `DRIFTED`, and `MISSING_LIVE` scans.
- Persist explanation state independently from scan execution: not requested, requested, saved, or failed.
- Return an existing saved explanation idempotently without another provider call.
- Reject non-completed/failed scan requests with a structured conflict.
- A failed Core explanation is terminal; there is no automatic or manual explanation retry.
- Scan status and deterministic outcome remain unchanged for every explanation state.

### OpenAI adapter

- Use the official TypeScript SDK, Responses API, and Structured Outputs.
- Read `OPENAI_API_KEY` and configurable `OPENAI_MODEL` server-side; document `gpt-5.6` as the initial value.
- Apply one bounded transport timeout and zero automatic retries.
- Validate structured fields: summary, important differences, likely implications, investigation checks, and limitations/uncertainty.
- Detect refusal, incomplete/invalid output, timeout, and provider errors and persist a safe explanation error.

### Sanitization

Provider input contains only:

- comparison outcome;
- supported desired/live replicas and image values;
- container/field identities and deterministic differences; and
- bounded operator-analysis instructions.

It excludes tokens, kubeconfig, repository authorization details, complete manifests, unrelated Kubernetes fields, raw logs/errors, history, and remediation tools.

### UI integration

- Show “Explain result” only for completed comparison outcomes.
- Require an explicit operator click.
- Show requested/loading, structured explanation, saved explanation, and failed states.
- Clearly label the content as AI-generated analysis and preserve the deterministic result above it.
- Do not add chat, charts, streaming text, or remediation controls.

## Non-goals

- AI drift classification, root-cause confirmation, remediation, or tool calls.
- Interactive chat or follow-up questions.
- Automatic explanation generation or retry.
- Full manifests, cluster inspection, or external retrieval by the model.
- Provider fallback or multi-model routing.
- Concurrent explanation-request coordination; Core only guarantees idempotent reuse after an explanation has been saved.

## Acceptance criteria

- Operator can manually request an explanation for each completed comparison outcome.
- Exactly one sanitized provider request occurs for a new explanation.
- Saved explanation survives restart and is returned without another call.
- Scan execution status/outcome never changes when explanation succeeds or fails.
- Provider payload contains only the allowlisted deterministic projection.
- Structured explanation renders all required operator-analysis sections.
- Refusal, invalid output, timeout, absent configuration, and provider failure produce safe persisted explanation errors.
- No automatic retry occurs.
- API/UI/logs never expose the OpenAI key or excluded scan data.

## Test evidence

- Happy: structured explanation saved and rendered for `IN_SYNC`, `DRIFTED`, and `MISSING_LIVE`.
- Edge: an already-saved explanation is returned idempotently without another provider call.
- Failures: refusal, malformed structured output, timeout, missing key/model, and provider error.
- Security: payload allowlist assertion and secret/log scan.
- Truth boundary: explicit assertions that scan status, outcome, and differences are byte-for-byte unchanged after every explanation path.
- Unit tests use a fake OpenAI adapter and no network.

## Documentation

Document server-side AI configuration, sanitized payload boundary, structured output, limitations, cost/provider dependency, no-retry behavior, and proof that AI is not drift truth.

## Rollback

Disable the explanation capability and revert the application commit while preserving existing deterministic scans. A persistence change must be additive or backward-safe; never delete scan history during rollback.

- Provide an idempotent script to create one named, single-node `kind` cluster with a pinned node image and bounded readiness wait.
- Create a dedicated namespace and least-privilege read-only credential/kubeconfig for DriftLens.
- RBAC permits only the Deployment read capability required by the configured target; no mutation through DriftLens credentials.
- DriftLens runs outside the cluster.

### One bounded demo sequence

Using the same cluster and configured manifest:

1. `IN_SYNC`: desired and live replicas/images match.
2. `DRIFTED`: controlled live replica and image changes produce exact differences.
3. `MISSING_LIVE`: delete the live Deployment and scan the desired manifest.
4. Failure and recovery: use an invalid configured source/path or bounded cluster-access failure, verify actionable failure in history, restore configuration/access, then start a normal successful scan. This is not retry.
5. Manually request and display one structured AI explanation for a completed drift outcome.

The demo setup may mutate its disposable cluster through explicit demo scripts; the DriftLens application and credential remain read-only.

### Local setup and final verification

- Clean-clone instructions cover prerequisites, configuration, kind setup, app startup, demo sequence, teardown, and common failures.
- One command or short documented command sequence runs lint, type, unit, build, integration, and the bounded operator flow.
- One real kind proof supplies live integration; do not duplicate cluster creation across normal unit/CI suites.
- Explanation-provider failure remains deterministic fake evidence rather than a required live-provider failure.

### Main deployment proof

- User-approved merge to protected `main` triggers the single verify → immutable build → deployment through the existing Proxmox/Cloudflare-protected path → exact-revision smoke DAG.
- Prove through the protected endpoint that the deployed version/health corresponds to the merge commit or artifact digest.
- Verify direct origin bypass is unavailable.
- A new or expanded Cloudflare route, access policy, domain, deployment identity, or Proxmox environment remains a separate user decision; private Git configuration remains Extended work.

### Submission package

- Comprehensive README: setup, use-case rationale, workflow, demo, API usage, testing, design decisions, security boundaries, trade-offs, limitations, and troubleshooting.
- Architecture overview finalized from PR #7.
- “What next” writeup maps MVP Extended/Future work and production hardening.
- Assessment matrix in PRD/release issue links exact evidence.
- Meaningful Git history review.
- Exact command, CI run URL, deployment SHA/digest, read-only RBAC, and demo evidence.
- Complete AI interaction inventory and full secret-reviewed exports for every user-facing session and delegated-agent prompt, relevant interaction, result, owner review, correction, and final outcome. Summaries do not replace full available transcripts. Use an explicit redaction manifest when needed, and carry forward any evidence blocker found by the #8 preflight.
- Useful screenshots or short recording for UI stages/outcomes if time remains.
- Final known-risk and failed-gate record.

## Non-goals

- New or expanded Cloudflare/Proxmox infrastructure, route, access policy, domain, or deployment permission.
- Private repository configuration or CRUD.
- CPU/memory resource drift.
- Cancellation, retry, timeout status, discovery, in-cluster DriftLens, or Extended scope.
- Production HA, backups, audit retention, or multi-user authentication.

## Acceptance criteria

- A clean clone completes the documented local setup.
- DriftLens UI and API execute a real read-only GitHub-to-kind scan.
- All four comparison/demo scenarios and actionable failure/recovery are retained in history.
- Replica and image differences are exact; extra live sidecars remain ignored if demonstrated/tested.
- Manual AI explanation works for a completed outcome; deterministic truth remains unchanged.
- Dedicated kubeconfig fails attempted Deployment mutation while required read succeeds.
- Full local quality pyramid passes on the final exact head.
- Protected-main merge automatically deploys and smoke-verifies the exact revision through the reused Cloudflare-protected endpoint.
- README, architecture, trade-offs, next-work, API, demo, and security documentation are complete.
- Every assessment requirement in #3 links retained evidence.
- Complete secret-safe user-facing and delegated-agent interaction exports are present, including prompts, available interaction/tool records, results, owner reviews, corrections, and final outcomes; summaries are not substituted for required full logs.
- The session inventory reconciles every delegation to an export location or an explicitly recorded submission blocker.
- Final repository secret scan and dependency audit pass.

## Test and evidence requirements

- Unit: happy, edge, and failure coverage for every changed module.
- Integration: SQLite/API contracts plus the one authorized real kind proof.
- End-to-end: one-worker, zero-retry Chromium critical operator flow.
- Security: read-only RBAC denial proof, workflow trust audit, credential/log/export scan.
- Delivery: GitHub Actions URLs, exact source SHA, artifact identity, deployment health/version, and rollback note.
- Documentation: commands executed from a clean clone or equivalent isolated checkout.

## Documentation

This issue owns the final README, demo guide, next-work writeup, assessment evidence index, AI-export inventory, and known-limitations/risk record.

## Rollback and teardown

Redeploy the last known-good immutable artifact if smoke fails. Preserve the SQLite evidence file unless corruption requires user-directed recovery. Demo-cluster teardown is explicit and targets only the named disposable cluster. Runner, environment, Cloudflare, DNS, credential, or other control-plane mutation or deletion beyond the approved reuse requires explicit user approval.

   424	
   425	## 16. Assessment deliverables and evidence
   115	- SQLite adapter: persist and retrieve the approved record projection.
   116	- OpenAI adapter: generate and validate a sanitized structured explanation.
   117	
   118	External client objects remain behind these adapters so unit tests can use
   119	deterministic fakes.
   120	
   121	## 4. Scan state flow
   122	
   123	One running process handles at most one active scan. A simple in-memory
   124	coordinator rejects a second start request with a structured conflict. This
   125	bounds resource use without adding durable leases, distributed locks, or
   126	concurrent-scan coordination.
   127	
   128	```mermaid
   129	stateDiagram-v2
   130	    [*] --> QUEUED: Persist scan
   131	    QUEUED --> RUNNING: Start asynchronous work
   132	    state RUNNING {
   133	        [*] --> LOADING_DESIRED
   134	        LOADING_DESIRED --> READING_LIVE
   135	        READING_LIVE --> COMPARING
   136	        COMPARING --> SAVING_RESULT
   137	    }
   138	    RUNNING --> COMPLETED
   139	    RUNNING --> FAILED
   140	```
   141	
   142	Explanation state is subordinate to, and independent of, scan execution:
   143	
   144	```mermaid
   145	stateDiagram-v2
   146	    [*] --> NOT_REQUESTED
   147	    NOT_REQUESTED --> REQUESTED: Manual operator action
   148	    REQUESTED --> SAVED
   149	    REQUESTED --> EXPLANATION_FAILED
   150	```
   151	
   152	The public execution statuses remain `QUEUED`, `RUNNING`, `COMPLETED`, and
   153	`FAILED`. Named running stages provide progress without creating additional
   154	execution statuses.
   155	
   156	The start request persists `QUEUED` before returning `202 Accepted`. A
   157	self-hosted Next.js Route Handler schedules
   158	`after(() => scanService.run(scanId))`; the long-lived Node.js process
   159	continues the scan while the UI polls. Core adds no interruption-recovery or
   160	shutdown-drain workflow and does not resume unfinished work after termination.
   161	
   162	Core has no overall workflow timeout, automatic retry, cancellation, or
   163	restart resumability. Each GitHub, Kubernetes, and OpenAI transport call still
   164	uses a bounded client or abort timeout so one hung dependency cannot occupy
   165	the sole active-scan slot indefinitely.
   166	
   167	After process restart, the in-memory active marker is empty. Any previously
   168	persisted `QUEUED` or `RUNNING` record remains unchanged as evidence; Core does
   169	not resume, complete, delete, or otherwise recover it. A new scan may start in
   170	the new process.
   171	
   172	An explanation is a separate manual operation available only for
   173	`IN_SYNC`, `DRIFTED`, and `MISSING_LIVE`. Explanation failure is persisted
   174	without changing the completed scan or deterministic outcome.

   176	## 5. Desired and live state
   177	
   178	### GitHub desired state
   179	
   180	Core uses native server-side `fetch` against the GitHub REST API:
   225	- ordered stage transitions needed by the Core progress display.

   235	explanation representation. SQLite does not implement an admission lease or
   236	advanced lock; the single-process coordinator owns the Core active-scan
   237	boundary.
   238	
   239	One idempotent schema bootstrap based on `PRAGMA user_version` and bounded
   240	`CREATE` statements runs during application startup. One connection serves
   241	the single process, and statements remain small and bounded. The database file
   242	lives on a persistent host path or container volume. SQLite fits one process
   243	and assessment-lifetime retention; an ORM, a general migration framework,
   244	PostgreSQL, and distributed coordination are deferred.
   245	
   290	  operator-controlled machine.
   291	- `kind` runs the private demo Kubernetes cluster.
   292	- The application reads a configured kubeconfig path.
   293	- SQLite uses a local persistent file.

   299	  deployment environment, initially on [REDACTED: PRIVATE TOPOLOGY] unless placement is changed

   304	- The existing Cloudflare-protected access path is reused for the [REDACTED: CREDENTIAL]

   310	
   311	## 9. Security and trust boundaries
   312	
   313	### Product runtime
   314	
   315	- Validate every API, configuration, manifest, and external response boundary.
   316	- Keep secrets in runtime configuration only.
   317	- Mask sensitive values in structured logs and errors.
   318	- Mount kubeconfig and deployment credentials read-only where possible.
   319	- Use least-privilege Kubernetes RBAC.
   320	- Restrict GitHub source identity and transport.
   321	- Never mutate Kubernetes.
   322	- Never expose the local origin publicly without the approved external access
   323	  boundary.
   324	
   325	Core has no application-managed authentication or authorization. Local mode
   326	relies on operator-controlled network placement; hosted access reuses the
   327	existing Cloudflare protection.
   328	
   329	### GitHub Actions
   330	
   331	This public repository uses self-hosted environments under a strict trust
   332	model:
   333	
   334	| Event | Self-hosted CI | Deployment access |
   335	| --- | --- | --- |
   336	| Push to canonical trusted issue branch | Allowed | None |
   337	| User-approved merge push to protected `main` | Full gates | Least-privilege demo deployment |
   338	| Fork or external pull-request event | Forbidden | Forbidden |
   339	| Comment or `pull_request_target` event | Forbidden | Forbidden |
   340	
   341	Workflows use canonical-repository `push` events only. External changes must be
   342	reviewed and copied into a trusted canonical branch before any execution.
   343	Workflow tokens are read-only by default, third-party Actions are pinned to
   344	immutable SHAs, and runner labels are not treated as a security boundary.
   345	
   346	CI and deployment need separate runner instances or isolated execution
   347	identities. CI must not have a deployment kubeconfig, Cloudflare credential,
   348	or broad home-lab access. The deployment identity accepts protected `main`
   349	pushes only.
   350	
   351	One workflow provides the delivery DAG:
   352	
   353	1. every trusted canonical branch push runs the verify job;
   354	2. the same `main` run continues to build one immutable SHA-tagged artifact;
   355	3. deployment waits for verify and build, then uses the isolated deployment
   356	   identity; and
   357	4. smoke verification proves the exact deployed revision.
   358	
   359	A single deployment concurrency group queues main revisions rather than
   360	cancelling an in-progress deployment. A second workflow must not duplicate the
   361	full verification or build.
   362	
   363	## 10. Observability and failure handling
   364	
   365	- Structured logs use levels and include scan and request correlation IDs.
   415	## 12. Trade-offs and deferred choices
   416	
   417	| Choice | Benefit | Accepted cost |
   418	| --- | --- | --- |
   419	| One TypeScript deployable | Fastest complete vertical workflow | Process boundaries are logical, not network-enforced |
   420	| In-process scan execution | No queue or worker operations | No restart resumability or horizontal scaling |
   421	| One active scan per process | Bounded behavior without advanced locks | No concurrent scans or durable admission lease |
   422	| Polling | Simple and observable | Repeated short API requests |
   423	| GitHub REST file retrieval | Narrow source and credential surface | GitHub-only; no full Git semantics |
   424	| SQLite | Durable history without another service | Single-instance persistence |
   425	| Node 24 `node:sqlite` | Minimal dependency surface | Release-candidate API stability |
   426	| Structured AI output | Stable UI/persistence contract | Provider and model dependency |
   427	| DriftLens outside Kubernetes | Simple local and hosted operation | No in-cluster identity in Core |
   428	| Self-hosted push-only CI | Uses existing home-lab delivery path | External PRs receive no automatic CI |
   429	
   430	Deferred work remains defined by PRD MVP Extended and Future scope. In
   431	particular: configuration CRUD, private repositories, resource quantities,
   432	cancel/timeout/manual retry, discovery, in-cluster ServiceAccount mode,
   433	new or expanded Proxmox/Cloudflare configuration, multiple clusters,
   434	scheduling, alerts, remediation, authentication, audit retention, and high
   435	availability. CPU and memory requests/limits are the first comparison
   436	enhancement after replicas and images pass.
   437	
   438	## 13. Dependency-ordered delivery slices
   439	
   440	1. Foundation and enforceable CI trust controls.
   441	2. Deterministic scan, API, persistence, and history.
   442	3. Focused operator UI and visible workflow state.
   443	4. Manual sanitized AI explanation.
   444	5. Local `kind` demo, hosted delivery, documentation, and submission evidence.
   445	
   446	Each slice receives a separate approved GitHub issue, worktree, branch, and
   447	pull request. Product implementation begins only after its issue specification
   448	is explicitly approved.
   449	
   450	At the owner-feedback checkpoint (`2026-07-30T20:48:31Z`), recorded assessment
   451	work is 84 minutes 36 seconds. The revised remaining-work targets below total
   452	146 minutes, leaving 9 minutes 24 seconds of the four-hour limit. They must be
   453	recalculated from the live ledger before the first implementation issue begins:
   454	
   455	| Slice | Target |
   456	| --- | ---: |
   457	| Foundation | 18 minutes |
   458	| Deterministic API and persistence | 47 minutes |
   459	| Operator UI | 27 minutes |
   460	| AI explanation | 12 minutes |
   461	| Demo, deployment, docs, and evidence | 42 minutes |
   462	| Risk reserve | 9 minutes 24 seconds |
   463	
   464	New Cloudflare/Proxmox infrastructure, private Git, configuration CRUD, and
   465	resource quantities do not begin inside this Core budget. Core only reuses the
   466	already configured hosted-delivery path.
   467

Every PRD acceptance item passes, every required child is merged through an explicitly user-approved exact head, the exact `main` revision is deployed and proven, and every assessment deliverable has retained secret-safe evidence linked here.","html_url":"https://github.com/RGCsAGupta/driftlens/issues/3","labels":["mvp:core","type:delivery"],"number":3,"state":"open","title":"[MVP Core] Ship the DriftLens engineering assessment"},{"assignees":["RGCsAGupta"],"body":"## Goal

Create the smallest locally runnable DriftLens application foundation and freeze the health, readiness, version, container, and quality contracts consumed by every product slice and the separate delivery path.

Parent: #3
Architecture: #4 and merged PR #7

## Operator and reviewer value

A clean clone runs a recognizable DriftLens shell locally and as a container, reports whether it is alive and ready, identifies its exact source revision, and has one reliable quality command before product behavior is added.

## Scope

### Application scaffold

- Next.js App Router with TypeScript strict mode and an npm lockfile.
- Node 24 pinned consistently for local, test, build, and container runtime.
- Minimal focused-console shell; no scan workflow UI yet.
- Health, readiness, and immutable build-version API responses with small documented contracts.
- Boundary validation for required non-secret configuration with safe actionable errors.
- Structured logging foundation with no credentials, PII, host details, or raw configuration values.
- Multi-stage production container image that runs as a non-root user and accepts an injected full commit SHA.
- Persistent-data mount contract reserved for later SQLite use without adding persistence in this issue.

### Quality foundation

- Formatting check, ESLint, strict type check, Vitest, changed-code coverage, production build, dependency audit, and secret-scan commands.
- Unit tests use no network.
- One top-level verification command executes the bounded local gate sequence.
- Baseline README instructions cover install, checks, local start, container build/run, and safe configuration.

### AI interaction evidence preflight

Before any implementation delegation, verify that the export process preserves each delegated-agent prompt, relevant interaction, result, owner review, correction, and final outcome. Start the session inventory and secret-review procedure. If complete delegated interactions cannot be exported, do not delegate implementation and record the submission blocker.

## Non-goals

- GitHub Actions, runner registration, branch protection, deployment environment, private registry, Proxmox, Cloudflare, or domain work; #13 owns the delivery path.
- Scan workflow, GitHub manifest loading, Kubernetes access, SQLite history, or OpenAI.
- Product UI beyond a recognizable shell.
- Kubernetes deployment of DriftLens.

## Acceptance criteria

- A clean clone succeeds with documented Node 24 and npm commands.
- Local UI, health, readiness, and build-version endpoints run with documented response semantics.
- Missing required non-secret configuration produces a safe readiness failure while liveness remains truthful.
- The production image builds, runs as non-root, and reports the injected exact 40-character commit SHA.
- Formatting, lint, type, unit, changed-code coverage, production build, dependency audit, and secret scan pass.
- Unit tests include happy, edge, and failure behavior for configuration and operational endpoints without network access.
- README documents only public-safe local and container setup.
- AI export preflight proves delegated interactions can be captured and secret-reviewed before delegation.
- No CI, repository-control, Proxmox, Cloudflare, or domain mutation occurs in this issue.

## Test evidence

- Happy: local and container health/readiness/version responses pass.
- Edge: optional configuration is absent without breaking liveness or leaking values.
- Failure: required non-secret configuration is invalid and readiness returns an actionable safe failure.
- Container: process is non-root and the build version exactly matches the injected SHA.

## Documentation

Update the README with foundation setup, commands, endpoint semantics, container use, required non-secret variables, and current limitations. Do not add a hosted URL or domain placeholder.

## Dependencies and parallelism

- Architecture PR #7 is merged.
- This issue owns the application contract required by #9 and #13.
- #13 may perform its read-only environment audit and workflow preparation in parallel, but its PR cannot be ready or merged until this issue is merged and it is rebased on the resulting contract.

## Rollback

Revert the application-foundation commit. There is no persistent schema or external control-plane mutation to roll back.

### API capabilities

- Start a scan and return `202` with scan identity and queued status.
- Retrieve one scan with status, stage transitions, target, resolved SHA, outcome, differences, and safe error.
- List bounded newest-first history with a default limit and enforced maximum.
- Return a structured conflict while another scan is active.
- Return non-secret configured source metadata needed by the UI.

Exact paths and Zod schemas are defined in the implementation and documented in the PR/README.

### Workflow

Persist and expose:

1. queued;
2. loading desired manifest;
3. reading live Deployment;
4. comparing supported fields;
5. saving result; and
6. completed or failed.

Use self-hosted Next.js `after()` for the in-process task. A simple in-memory coordinator admits at most one active scan in the current process and returns conflict for a second request. There is no automatic retry, cancellation, overall workflow timeout, concurrent-scan support, advanced locking, or restart resumability. Every external transport call has a bounded timeout.

### Desired state

- Resolve branch/SHA through GitHub REST.
- Fetch exactly one file at the resolved SHA.
- Plain YAML, one document, one `apps/v1` Deployment.
- Require explicit name and namespace.
- Reject unsafe path, wrong kind/version, multiple documents, or malformed manifest.

### Live state and comparison

- Read exactly the matching namespaced Deployment with `@kubernetes/client-node`.
- Use read-only Kubernetes access; perform no list/watch/write operation.
- Compare `spec.replicas`, defaulting omitted desired replicas to `1`.
- Match desired regular containers by name and compare exact image strings.
- Desired container missing live reports drift.
- Extra live-only containers are ignored.
- Init/ephemeral containers and unrelated/runtime-owned fields are ignored.
- Produce only `IN_SYNC`, `DRIFTED`, or `MISSING_LIVE` as comparison outcomes.
- Git, manifest, authorization, availability, timeout, and internal failures produce typed execution errors, never drift.

### Persistence

Use Node 24 `node:sqlite` with one idempotent schema-version-1 `PRAGMA user_version` bootstrap, one connection, a scan record, and append-only stage records. All dynamic values use prepared, parameterized statements; only fixed schema bootstrap statements may execute as static SQL.

Persist only PRD-approved projections, differences, timestamps, resolved SHA, outcome, and safe errors. Never persist complete manifests, kubeconfig, credentials, or unrelated fields.

A bootstrap or initial scan write failure releases the in-memory coordinator, returns a safe synchronous service error, and creates no scan. After the queued scan is persisted, terminal failure persistence is best effort: if SQLite itself cannot write the terminal record, readiness, correlated structured logs, and the API expose a safe storage failure without claiming that failed history was durably recorded. Core does not resume the stale workflow automatically.

The coordinator exists only in the current process. Restart clears that marker; any prior `QUEUED` or `RUNNING` record remains unchanged as evidence. Core does not resume, complete, delete, or otherwise recover it, and the new process may start a new scan.

## Non-goals

- Operator workflow UI beyond API inspection.
- AI explanation.
- CPU or memory quantities.
- Configuration CRUD or private Git.
- Detailed event log, cancellation, retry, timeout status, or restart recovery.
- Discovery, scheduling, remediation, or additional Kubernetes resources.
- Live kind proof; the release issue supplies the single bounded live demo.

## Acceptance criteria

- Starting a valid scan returns immediately and stage/status polling observes persisted progress.
- Branch input resolves and stores its immutable commit SHA.
- `IN_SYNC` is exact for matching replicas and every desired container image.
- Replica drift, image drift, and missing desired containers produce field-level differences.
- Extra live-only containers do not produce drift.
- Kubernetes 404 becomes `MISSING_LIVE` and a completed scan.
- Invalid manifest, unsupported resource, Git failure, Kubernetes denial/unavailability, and transport timeout are actionable persisted execution failures when storage remains available.
- Bootstrap/initial-scan storage failure returns synchronously without a scan; later storage failure is exposed safely without a false durable-history claim.
- History survives application restart and returns bounded newest-first results.
- A concurrent start attempt returns conflict without creating a second active workflow.
- After restart, the new in-memory coordinator admits a new scan and leaves any stale prior record unchanged.
- API responses and logs contain no credentials or complete manifests.

## Test evidence

- Unit happy: replicas/images in sync.
- Unit edges: omitted replicas, name-based reordered containers, extra live sidecar ignored, missing desired container, multiple differences.
- Unit failures: malformed/multi-document/wrong-resource manifest and safe error mapping.
- Workflow happy: fake GitHub/Kubernetes adapters drive every stage to persisted completion.
- Workflow failures: each adapter/stage failure persists the correct terminal error; no automatic retry calls occur.
- Persistence: version-1 bootstrap idempotency, prepared-statement binding, injection-safe dynamic values, ordered stages, restart history, and bounded query.
- Storage failures: bootstrap/initial-scan failure creates no scan; later write failure proves best-effort terminal handling plus safe readiness, log, and API evidence.
- Restart coordinator: a new process can start a scan while the stale prior record remains neither resumed, completed, deleted, nor modified.
- API: validation, `202`, polling detail, history, not-found, and active conflict.
- Security: fake Kubernetes client asserts read-only Deployment operation and sanitized persistence/logging.

## Documentation

Document non-secret configuration, API capability examples, comparison semantics, error taxonomy, persistence boundary, and Core limitations.

## Rollback

Revert the application commit and redeploy the last known-good artifact. Database bootstrap must be backward-safe for this issue; if a schema rollback is unsafe, preserve the file and document recovery rather than deleting history.

- Reject non-completed/failed scan requests with a structured conflict.

### OpenAI adapter

- Use the official TypeScript SDK, Responses API, and Structured Outputs.
- Read `OPENAI_API_KEY` and configurable `OPENAI_MODEL` server-side; document `gpt-5.6` as the initial value.
- Apply one bounded transport timeout and zero automatic retries.
- Validate structured fields: summary, important differences, likely implications, investigation checks, and limitations/uncertainty.
- Detect refusal, incomplete/invalid output, timeout, and provider errors and persist a safe explanation error.

### Sanitization

Provider input contains only:

- comparison outcome;
- supported desired/live replicas and image values;
- container/field identities and deterministic differences; and
- bounded operator-analysis instructions.

It excludes tokens, kubeconfig, repository authorization details, complete manifests, unrelated Kubernetes fields, raw logs/errors, history, and remediation tools.

### UI integration

- Show “Explain result” only for completed comparison outcomes.
- Require an explicit operator click.
- Show requested/loading, structured explanation, saved explanation, and failed states.

- Automatic explanation generation or retry.

- Concurrent explanation-request coordination; Core only guarantees idempotent reuse after an explanation has been saved.

- Scan execution status/outcome never changes when explanation succeeds or fails.
- Provider payload contains only the allowlisted deterministic projection.
- Structured explanation renders all required operator-analysis sections.
- Refusal, invalid output, timeout, absent configuration, and provider failure produce safe persisted explanation errors.
- No automatic retry occurs.
- API/UI/logs never expose the OpenAI key or excluded scan data.

## Test evidence

- Happy: structured explanation saved and rendered for `IN_SYNC`, `DRIFTED`, and `MISSING_LIVE`.
- Edge: an already-saved explanation is returned idempotently without another provider call.
- Failures: refusal, malformed structured output, timeout, missing key/model, and provider error.
- Security: payload allowlist assertion and secret/log scan.
- Truth boundary: explicit assertions that scan status, outcome, and differences are byte-for-byte unchanged after every explanation path.
- Unit tests use a fake OpenAI adapter and no network.

## Documentation

Document server-side AI configuration, sanitized payload boundary, structured output, limitations, cost/provider dependency, no-retry behavior, and proof that AI is not drift truth.

## Rollback

Disable the explanation capability and revert the application commit while preserving existing deterministic scans. A persistence change must be additive or backward-safe; never delete scan history during rollback.

Establish DriftLens’s trusted CI and private deployment path independently from product development, reusing the existing self-hosted Proxmox and Cloudflare infrastructure without selecting or configuring a DriftLens domain yet.

Parent: #3
Architecture: #4 and merged PR #7

## Operator and reviewer value

A trusted canonical-repository push is verified, built as an immutable artifact, and deployed to the existing private Proxmox environment with exact-revision health evidence. Product work can proceed independently without mixing infrastructure control changes into application PRs.

## Scope

### Read-only environment audit and reuse

- Inspect the existing [REDACTED: PRIVATE TOPOLOGY] self-hosted CI and deployment environments, identities, private registry access, Proxmox application runtime, and shared Cloudflare tunnel/proxy/access infrastructure.
- Reuse working Restaurant OS delivery patterns where they fit; do not copy application-specific configuration.
- Verify whether DriftLens needs only repository bindings and a dedicated application deployment target.
- Stop for a new user decision if work requires a new runner host, execution identity, registry authority, Cloudflare account/tunnel/access policy, Proxmox environment, or broader permission.
- Never record runner names, host addresses, internal DNS, credentials, kubeconfig values, or secret material in public issues, commits, logs, or AI exports.

Live planning baseline at 2026-07-30: DriftLens has no registered repository runner, only the default GitHub Pages environment, and no main-branch protection. Recheck all three before implementation because repository state can change.

### Trusted GitHub Actions path

- Use canonical-repository `push` events only.
- Trusted issue branches run the [REDACTED: CREDENTIAL] chain without deployment access.
- Protected `main` runs verify, immutable build/publish, private deploy, and exact-revision smoke automatically after a user-approved merge.
- No `pull_request`, `pull_request_target`, issue-comment, fork, external-contributor, dependency-bot, schedule, or manual-dispatch execution on self-hosted runners in Core.
- Workflow permissions are read-only by default, all third-party Actions are pinned to full commit SHAs, jobs have bounded timeouts, and dependency caching never restores mutable `node_modules`.
- CI and deployment use separate identities/labels. CI cannot access registry publisher credentials, deployment SSH material, kubeconfig, Cloudflare credentials, or broad home-lab resources.
- Deployment is restricted to `main` through a DriftLens GitHub environment and one non-cancelling concurrency group.

### Immutable private deployment

- Consume the health, readiness, build-version, and container contracts delivered by #8.
- Build and publish one immutable image tagged with the full Git commit SHA; never deploy `latest`.
- Use pinned SSH host trust, batch mode, a least-privilege deployment identity, and a release tied to the exact SHA.
- Keep persistent DriftLens data outside the replaceable release/image lifecycle.
- Verify private health, readiness, and exact build version after deployment.
- Retain the previous immutable image/release for bounded application rollback.
- Remove transient registry and SSH material from the runner after every outcome.

### Domain and Cloudflare boundary

- Reuse the existing shared Cloudflare tunnel/proxy/access infrastructure; do not create a new account, tunnel, or access policy.
- Do not guess, reserve, hardcode, or publish a DriftLens hostname or domain in this issue.
- Keep the origin private and do not add public router port forwarding.
- The user supplies the domain only in release issue #12. That issue owns the domain-specific route, protected external health/version smoke, and direct-origin-bypass proof.

### Restaurant OS patterns intentionally reused

- Separate CI and deployment identities.
- Immutable full-SHA image/release identity.
- Pinned SSH trust and least-privilege remote deployment.
- Non-interruptible production concurrency.
- Private health/version verification, last-known-good rollback, and transient credential cleanup.
- Static tests that enforce workflow trust and deployment invariants.

DriftLens intentionally omits Restaurant OS migration, database backup/restore, email/provider credential handoff, multi-runner capacity, scheduled regression, and large Compose-stack machinery.

## Non-goals

- Application scaffold or product features.
- Domain selection, hostname route, or public Cloudflare smoke.
- New infrastructure or expanded home-lab authority.
- Kubernetes demo-cluster creation or DriftLens Kubernetes deployment.
- Production HA, autoscaling, backups, or zero-downtime orchestration.
- External/fork pull-request CI on self-hosted runners.

## Acceptance criteria

- Read-only audit distinguishes reusable configuration, missing DriftLens bindings, and any decision-gated gap without exposing sensitive values.
- Static workflow-policy tests prove the allowed trigger set, read-only defaults, immutable action pins, CI/deploy separation, full-SHA artifact, no `latest`, bounded timeouts, and non-cancelling deployment.
- A trusted canonical issue-branch push runs verification without deployment credentials or deployment steps.
- Fork/PR/comment/manual events cannot schedule a DriftLens self-hosted job by workflow inspection and repository settings.
- `main` blocks direct push, force-push, and deletion and requires the verified check before merge.
- A user-approved merge to `main` deploys the exact immutable revision privately and verifies health, readiness, and build version.
- A controlled failure prevents success claims and preserves the last known-good private deployment.
- No domain, hostname, host address, runner identity, credential, or secret appears in public evidence.
- No Cloudflare domain route is created before the user supplies the domain in #12.

## Test evidence

- Happy: canonical branch verification and exact-main private deployment contract.
- Edge: superseded deployment remains non-interruptible and only the newest pending deployment may continue.
- Failure: health/readiness/version mismatch fails deployment proof and retains/restores the last known-good application revision.
- Security: static workflow tests, repository-setting audit, runner-identity separation, pinned-host verification, and secret/log scan.

## Documentation

Document only public-safe prerequisites, the trust boundary, the private deployment flow, rollback, and the explicit domain gate. Correct PRD/architecture wording so Core reuses existing Cloudflare infrastructure while hostname binding waits for #12.

## Dependencies and parallelism

- Read-only infrastructure audit and workflow preparation may proceed in parallel with #8 in a separate worktree and PR.
- The delivery PR cannot be ready or merged until #8’s health/readiness/version/container contract is merged and the branch is rebased on it.
- #12 depends on this issue for final domain-bound release proof.

## Rollback

Redeploy the last known-good immutable revision. Repository settings, runner bindings, environments, credentials, Proxmox resources, or Cloudflare controls may be reverted or removed only with explicit user approval.

   332	model:

   335	| --- | --- | --- |

{"body":"## Goal\n\nDeliver the focused operator console that consumes the scan APIs and makes initiation, progress, deterministic results, history, and failures transparent.\n\nParent: #3\nArchitecture: #4 and PR #7\nDepends on: #8 and #9\nTarget budget: 25 active minutes, recalculated before implementation.\n\n## Operator value\n\nA platform engineer or SRE can complete and understand the real DriftLens workflow without inspecting raw API payloads or logs.\n\n## Scope\n\n### Console shell\n\n- Show DriftLens purpose and configured public repository/manifest path without exposing credentials.\n- Provide one branch-or-SHA input and primary “Run scan” action.\n- Disable or replace the action with an explicit busy state while a scan is active.\n- Remain a focused console, not a monitoring dashboard.\n\n### Progress and outcome\n\n- Poll the backend while the scan is queued/running.\n- Show current [REDACTED: CREDENTIAL] and terminal execution status.\n- Present `IN_SYNC`, `DRIFTED`, and `MISSING_LIVE` distinctly without using color alone.\n- For drift, show a compact field-level table with field/container identity, desired value, and live value.\n- Show resolved commit SHA and Deployment namespace/name.\n- Render actionable safe failure text with a stable error category.\n\n### History\n\n- Show bounded newest-first history with time, target, execution status, and comparison outcome.\n- Open a previous scan without starting another workflow.\n- Refresh history after terminal completion.\n- Preserve selected scan identity in the URL where practical; do not use browser local storage.\n\n### Interaction and accessibility\n\n- Keyboard-operable controls, visible focus, labeled form input, semantic status text, and accessible loading indication.\n- Responsive layout for normal laptop widths.\n- Prevent duplicate submissions and stale polling updates.\n- Stop polling at a terminal state and show safe retry-by-new-scan guidance for failures; no retry feature is implemented.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n- Repository or target configuration UI.\n- AI explanation controls; issue #11 adds them.\n- Charts, trends, monitoring dashboard, bulk actions, or live streaming.\n- Cancellation, retry, timeout, discovery, authentication, or multi-user behavior.\n- Full manifest display or raw error/log viewer.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Operator can start a real scan through the API from the UI.\n- Every Core stage is visibly understandable while polling.\n- In-sync, replica drift, image drift, missing live, and failed execution render correctly.\n- Drift table displays exact supported desired/live values and container names.\n- History and previous details remain usable after page reload without local storage.\n- Active scan prevents duplicate submission.\n- Polling stops on completion/failure and does not overwrite a newly selected history item.\n- UI never displays secrets, kubeconfig, tokens, complete manifests, or unsafe backend details.\n- Layout and controls pass the agreed [REDACTED: CREDENTIAL] checks.\n\n## Test evidence\n\n- Component happy: queued → stages → completed in-sync.\n- Component edges: multiple replica/image differences, missing live, empty history, and long safe messages.\n- Component failure: backend validation/execution error and polling transport failure remain actionable.\n- Parameterized rendering test covers status/outcome/history variants without duplicated suites.\n- One-worker, zero-retry Chromium Playwright flow covers start, progress, result, and history using controlled adapters.\n- Accessibility smoke covers labels, roles, focus, keyboard operation, and non-color status cues.\n- Production build and existing backend suites remain green.\n\n## Documentation\n\nAdd operator workflow screenshots only when stable and useful. Update README usage, visible statuses, and UI limitations.\n\n## Rollback\n\nRevert the UI commit and redeploy the last known-good artifact. No persistence migration is introduced by this issue.\n","labels":["spec:needs-review","mvp:core","type:feature"],"url":"https://github.com/RGCsAGupta/driftlens/issues/10"}
{"body":"## Goal\n\nAllow the operator to manually request and persist a short structured explanation for every completed comparison outcome without letting AI determine or alter drift.\n\nParent: #3\nArchitecture: #4 and PR #7\nDepends on: #8, #9, and #10\nTarget budget: 10 active minutes, recalculated before implementation.\n\n## Operator value\n\nAn operator receives concise analysis of deterministic differences, implications, investigation checks, and uncertainty while retaining the exact field-level result as source of truth.\n\n## Scope\n\n### Explanation API and state\n\n- Add a manual explanation request capability for completed `IN_SYNC`, `DRIFTED`, and `MISSING_LIVE` scans.\n- Persist explanation state independently from scan execution: not requested, requested, saved, or failed.\n- Return an existing saved explanation idempotently without another provider call.\n- Reject non-completed/failed scan requests with a structured conflict.\n- A failed Core explanation is terminal; there is no automatic or manual explanation retry.\n- Scan status and deterministic outcome remain unchanged for every explanation state.\n\n### OpenAI adapter\n\n- Use the official TypeScript SDK, Responses API, and Structured Outputs.\n- Read `OPENAI_API_KEY` and configurable `OPENAI_MODEL` server-side; document `gpt-5.6` as the initial value.\n- Apply one bounded transport timeout and zero automatic retries.\n- Validate structured fields: summary, important differences, likely implications, investigation checks, and limitations/uncertainty.\n- Detect refusal, incomplete/invalid output, timeout, and provider errors and persist a safe explanation error.\n\n### Sanitization\n\nProvider input contains only:\n\n- comparison outcome;\n- supported desired/live replicas and image values;\n- container/field identities and deterministic differences; and\n- bounded operator-analysis instructions.\n\nIt excludes tokens, kubeconfig, repository authorization details, complete manifests, unrelated Kubernetes fields, raw logs/errors, history, and remediation tools.\n\n### UI integration\n\n- Show “Explain result” only for completed comparison outcomes.\n- Require an explicit operator click.\n- Show requested/loading, structured explanation, saved explanation, and failed states.\n- Clearly label the content as AI-generated analysis and preserve the deterministic result above it.\n- Do not add chat, charts, streaming text, or remediation controls.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n- AI drift classification, root-cause confirmation, remediation, or tool calls.\n- Interactive chat or follow-up questions.\n- Automatic explanation generation or retry.\n- Full manifests, cluster inspection, or external retrieval by the model.\n- Provider fallback or multi-model routing.\n- Concurrent explanation-request coordination; Core only guarantees idempotent reuse after an explanation has been saved.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Operator can manually request an explanation for each completed comparison outcome.\n- One accepted non-concurrent manual request makes one sanitized provider call; a saved explanation makes no further call, and concurrent duplicate requests have no Core exactly-once guarantee.\n- Saved explanation survives restart and is returned without another call.\n- Scan execution status/outcome never changes when explanation succeeds or fails.\n- Provider payload contains only the allowlisted deterministic projection.\n- Structured explanation renders all required operator-analysis sections.\n- Refusal, invalid output, timeout, absent configuration, and provider failure produce safe persisted explanation errors.\n- No automatic retry occurs.\n- API/UI/logs never expose the OpenAI key or excluded scan data.\n\n## Test evidence\n\n- Happy: structured explanation saved and rendered for `IN_SYNC`, `DRIFTED`, and `MISSING_LIVE`.\n- Edge: an already-saved explanation is returned idempotently without another provider call.\n- Failures: refusal, malformed structured output, timeout, missing key/model, and provider error.\n- Security: payload allowlist assertion and secret/log scan.\n- Truth boundary: explicit assertions that scan status, outcome, and differences are byte-for-byte unchanged after every explanation path.\n- Unit tests use a fake OpenAI adapter and no network.\n\n## Documentation\n\nDocument server-side AI configuration, sanitized payload boundary, structured output, limitations, cost/provider dependency, no-retry behavior, and proof that AI is not drift truth.\n\n## Rollback\n\nDisable the explanation capability and revert the application commit while preserving existing deterministic scans. A persistence change must be additive or backward-safe; never delete scan history during rollback.\n\n\n\n\n","labels":["spec:needs-review","mvp:core","type:feature"],"url":"https://github.com/RGCsAGupta/driftlens/issues/11"}
